claims.claim: Structurally related heteroaryl-aniline contexts report absolute oral bioavailability well above 20% in humans: GSK1322322 57–77%, R406 54.6%, ZL-2201 ~70%, brepocitinib 75%, deucravacitinib 99%, and nilotinib 31% under fasted conditions.

New L2 records reinforce the positive direction: ZL-2201 F was 115% in monkeys and 134% in mice; brepocitinib is described as orally bioavailable with dose-dependent increases; phenserine rat F was 100%; nilotinib remained ~31% fasted; and isradipine/propranolol cirrhosis values remained above 20%.
No active record provides affirmative evidence of F < 20% for the query or for a transferable context; the lowest relevant measured F is nilotinib at 31% fasted, still above the threshold.

The unfavorable physicochemical prior (MW 585, logP 5.08, low neutral fraction, high TPSA) is not endpoint proof and is outweighed by multiple transferable positive absolute-bioavailability contexts and the absence of affirmative low-F evidence.

evidence_gaps: No direct absolute oral bioavailability measurement for the query molecule; prediction relies on transfer from analog contexts.
No data on the query's isopropyl ester stability/prodrug behavior, acrylamide reactivity, first-pass metabolism, or formulation.
No fasted/fed or dose condition is specified for the query; fed/fasted can alter F (e.g., GSK1322322 57% fasted vs 77% fed).
Physicochemical liabilities (MW 585, logP 5.08, TPSA 114, low neutral fraction) could reduce absorption but are not affirmative threshold evidence.
